routes.description: Establish that libertarian sourcehood remains coherent under non-causal determination and that Bradleyan idealism accommodates agency, normativity, feeling, and inquiry without reducing reality to natural-scientific description.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by distinguishing logical determination from causal constraint, preserving meaningful alternatives and agential influence, and showing that Bradleyan idealism explains experiential and normative dimensions that reductive naturalism or pragmatic reconstruction leaves incomplete.

motionBridge.description: Show that libertarian agency joined to Bradleyan idealism answers determinist and naturalist pressures more comprehensively than compatibilist pragmatism.

centralBridges.description: Establish agential sourcehood and alternative possibility without requiring an objectively branching future or confusing logical implication with causal control.
Explain how reasoning and deliberation remain answerable to normative standards rather than becoming merely compelled psychological sequences.
Show why an adequate metaphysics must integrate scientific truth with agency, feeling, value, and experience instead of treating scientific description as exhaustive.
Ground the intelligibility and direction of inquiry in a real idealist completion joining knower and known, not solely in a useful regulative practice.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Demonstrate that indeterminacy, top-down constraint, or level-relative explanation can make libertarian alternatives coherent even within physicalist models.
Specify experiential, operational, and intellectual constraints that prevent idealist truth from becoming arbitrary or voluntarily constructed.

routes.description: Establish that non-causal determinism preserves the practical distinctions constituting free agency and that naturalistically acceptable, experience-centered pragmatism captures inquiry and progress without Bradleyan metaphysical commitments.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by showing that fixed laws and past conditions still pressure libertarian alternatives, that functional freedom supports deliberative and responsibility practices, and that pragmatic standards explain experience and inquiry without requiring an independently real absolute.

motionBridge.description: Show that compatibilist pragmatism answers the relevant determinist and naturalist pressures without the additional modal and metaphysical commitments of libertarian idealism.

centralBridges.description: Maintain the fixed-past challenge by distinguishing broad possible-world variation from the ability to act otherwise with the actual past and laws held fixed.
Define freedom through action-guiding distinctions involving reasons-responsiveness, coercion, prediction, incentives, praise, and blame under determinism.
Account for experience as inquiry's subject matter and physical objects as experiential models without inferring anti-naturalism or conscious control of reality.
Supply constrained standards for intellectual, moral, and aesthetic progress while testing whether a real Bradleyan absolute adds necessary explanation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate predictability from causal puppeteering while identifying the pressure complete external predictability places on libertarian branching.
Test whether an inaccessible unstructured feeling can support Bradleyan metaphysics when reflective perception is already categorically structured.

sections.title: Determinism, Alternative Possibilities, and Sourcehood
sections.rationale: This issue contains the principal modal clash over fixed pasts and laws, branching possibilities, logical determination, causal control, and whether agents can remain genuine sources.

sections.title: Normative Reasoning and Practical Freedom
sections.rationale: This issue connects the alleged self-undermining consequences of compelled reasoning with the compatibilist account of freedom through deliberation, responsibility, and socially useful distinctions.

sections.title: Naturalism, Reduction, and Experience
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether scientific explanation exhausts reality or whether experience, agency, feeling, morality, and aesthetics require the broader resources claimed for Bradleyan idealism.

sections.title: Idealist Truth, Feeling, and Perceptual Structure
sections.rationale: This issue tests how idealism constrains truth, whether precognitive feeling can ground thought, and whether unavoidable categorization supports or pressures Bradley's account of experience.

sections.title: The Absolute, Inquiry, and Pragmatic Standards
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether inquiry presupposes a genuinely real idealist completion or only a regulative commitment to progress, and what standards prevent either reductionism or unrestricted metaphysical admission.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: Causal determinism threatens rational normativity because beliefs and inferences that are merely caused cannot remain answerable to independent standards of correct reasoning.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: Logical and mathematical relations provide mind-independent standards for how agents ought to reason, preserving a distinction between valid inference and psychologically caused thought.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: Time-symmetric physical equations establish mathematical interconnection but do not establish that temporally prior states causally constrain or force later choices.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c05.proposition: Libertarian freedom requires both agential sourcehood and alternative possibility, but the relevant alternatives can exist across possible worlds without an objectively branching future.

chunk-003:c003-05.proposition: Bradleyan idealism accepts scientific truths while denying that they exhaust reality, requiring metaphysics also to integrate agential, moral, aesthetic, religious, and felt experience.

chunk-003:c003-06.proposition: Reality is richer than intellectual thought because feeling and volition precede systematic reflection, while science deliberately abstracts from agential, ethical, and aesthetic value.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-02.proposition: Bradleyan truth combines operational coherence with constraints from felt reality and intellectual satisfaction, so false claims encounter practical failure rather than becoming true by choice.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-03.proposition: Although reflective agents cannot recover wholly unstructured experience, precognitive feeling remains thought's foundation and is ultimately integrated with thought and volition in the absolute.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-05.proposition: The normative drive toward fulfilled truth treats complete reality as more real than present partial understanding, so Bradley's absolute is not merely a convenient regulative fiction.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-07.proposition: Inquiry presupposes an intelligible attainable end, and idealism explains that intelligibility by joining knower and known within experience rather than positing wholly inaccessible independent reality.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-10.proposition: Even without causal necessitation, fixed laws and a fixed physical state that uniquely determine later states undermine libertarian branching alternatives.

chunk-002:chunk-002-c08.proposition: Possible worlds with different pasts establish a broader ability to do otherwise than the consequence argument tests, which holds the actual past and laws fixed.

chunk-003:c003-02.proposition: Non-causal determinism provides a basis for compatibilism because complete predictability need not amount to causal puppeteering or compulsion.

chunk-003:c003-03.proposition: Free will is functionally constituted by distinctions used to guide incentives, prediction, praise, and blame, which remain meaningful in a deterministic society.

chunk-003:c003-07.proposition: An experience-centered idealism can remain naturalistically acceptable by treating experience as inquiry's subject matter and physical objects as useful models of experience.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-01.proposition: Although idealism need not imply voluntary control over reality, Bradley's unstructured felt real is pressured by the categorization already built into accessible perception.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-04.proposition: Bradley's absolute requires clarification between a regulative ideal that guides inquiry and an independently real endpoint whose existence adds a substantive metaphysical commitment.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-09.proposition: A defensible anti-reductionism requires pragmatic admission standards that avoid both scientistic exclusion and an unrestricted metaphysical free-for-all.
